rejected.title: The Treaty of Versailles
card: The Treaty of Versailles was the peace treaty signed with Germany in 1919. Germany had to sign it and had no say in its terms.
Blame
Germany had to accept responsibility for causing the war. This was set out in what is known as the war guilt clause.
Reparations
Germany had to pay money to the winners to cover the cost of war damage.
Germany also lost land, including some territory in Europe and its overseas colonies, and its army was cut to a small size. Many Germans saw the treaty as harsh and unfair.
rejected.remember: Versailles made Germany accept blame, pay, lose land and cut its army, and many Germans resented it.

a.q: Which of these was a term of the Treaty of Versailles?
opts: Germany had to accept blame for the war
Germany was allowed to keep a large army
Germany helped write the terms of the treaty
Germany gained land from its neighbours
a.why: Under the war guilt clause, Germany had to accept blame for the war. Germany's army was cut, it lost land, and it had no say in the terms, so the other three options are wrong.
a.clue: Three options treat Germany more gently than the treaty did.

b.q: In 1920, a German veteran complains that the treaty was a peace dictated to Germany. Which part of the treaty is he pointing to?
opts: Germany had no say in the terms it signed
Germany had to pay money for war damage
Germany lost its colonies overseas
Germany's army was cut to a small size
b.why: A dictated peace is one handed over with no chance to negotiate, and Germany had no say in the terms. Paying reparations, losing colonies and cutting the army were all real terms, but they describe what the treaty said, not how it was made.
b.clue: His complaint is about how the deal was made, not what it said.

a.q: Which of these was a term of the Treaty of Versailles?
opts: Germany had to accept blame for the war
Germany was allowed to keep a large army
Germany was asked to take part in writing the terms
Germany gained land from its neighbours
a.why: Germany had to accept blame under the war guilt clause. It lost land, its army was cut, and it had no say in the terms, so the other options are wrong.
a.clue: The treaty placed responsibility on the defeated side.

b.q: Why did many Germans resent the treaty?
opts: They had to sign it, accept blame and lose land and troops
It left Germany's army larger than before the war
It cancelled all payments owed to the winners
It was written with Germany's leaders as equals
b.why: Germans had no say in the terms, were blamed for the war, and lost land and soldiers, so many felt it was unfair. It did not cancel payments, since reparations were a main term.
b.clue: Think about what Germany lost and what it was forced to accept.

a.best: Germany had to accept blame for the war

b.best: They had to sign it, accept blame and lose land and troops
